One Tag Per Line Each # annotation must be on its own line directly above the field. Never combine tags on one line. No Fixed Scale on Measures Use # currency (no scale) on measure definitions. The same measure renders at many granularities: usd0m turns $500 into $0.0M. Add scale (e.g., # currency=usd0m) only in views after confirming value ranges with queries. # bigvalue Needs # label on Each Measure Without # label, bigvalue cards show raw field names which are often unclear. Sparkline Sparklines in # bigvalue require TWO things: a # hidden nested view AND a .sparkline= reference. If the sparkline doesn't show: check that # hidden is on the nested view AND the view name matches .sparkline=. Comparison Deltas Use downisgood=true for metrics where decrease is positive (churn, defects).

readme_snippet: Maton API Gateway Managed API routing for third-party apps, provided by Maton. NPM Homebrew Authentication Prints a login link. The CLI reads them when it needs them. Verify If authenticated is false, stop and login again via maton login. If authtype is apikey, it is recommended to login via maton login and avoid keeping a long-lived credential. Connections List Connections Refer to maton connection list --help for possible flags and values. Create Connection Requires explicit user approval. readme_snippet: DNS DNS is the global front door: it turns a name (api.example.com) into an address before any request reaches your servers. It is also a routing layer — the same lookup can hand different clients different answers (by region, latency, health, or weight). Get it wrong and clients reach a dead region, fail over in minutes instead of seconds, or cache a bad answer for hours. It is not a load balancer and not a CDN; it decides which endpoint a client is told to use, not how bytes are balanced inside that endpoint. When to reach for this A service is reachable by a stable hostname; traffic must be steered to the closest or healthiest region/data center; or an endpoint's IP can change (a new load balancer, a failover site) and clients must follow without code changes. Multi-region or multi-data-center designs need DNS to pick the entry point; single-region designs still need it for a stable, movable name.

ALL imports from react-server-dom-webpack/ (Flight server/static APIs) must go through entry-base.ts. name: saga
description: Run an autonomous, spec-driven development "saga" for medium-to-large features using an orchestrator agent and a fleet of worker subagents. Use this skill whenever the user invokes /saga, asks to autonomously build a sizable feature end-to-end with minimal human intervention, wants a comprehensive spec broken into milestones and tasks with airtight validation criteria before parallelized implementation, or wants an orchestrator to delegate implementation to worker agents while preserving its own context window. Trigger on phrases like "run a saga", "autonomously implement this feature", "spec it out then build it with subagents", "orchestrate this big feature end-to-end", or "build this with workers and validate each step". Also use this skill when asked to continue, resume, or pick up an existing saga from its saga directory (e.g. under ~/.sagas).
readme_snippet: Saga Saga is an autonomous, spec-driven development workflow for medium-to-large features that should be implemented mostly without human intervention, except at a few discrete touch points. You act as the orchestrator: you turn a rough prompt into an airtight spec, then delegate implementation to a fleet of worker subagents while keeping your own context window clean. The whole method rests on one bet: if the spec defines every task with validation criteria tight enough to form a contract, then workers can execute in parallel and self-verify, and the saga succeeds with almost no human babysitting. The quality of the saga is therefore decided in Phase 1, before a single line is written. Core principles Airtight contracts over good intentions. A task is only ready to delegate when its validation criteria are so explicit that meeting them leaves little-to-no possibility the task was done wrong. Ambiguity is the enemy; resolve it during planning, not during implementation. No whitespace.

name: awesome-literature-review
description: 中文学术文献综述全流程生成。分四部分(研究背景与目的、文献梳理与分析、研究现状总结与评述、参考文献),开场先对齐题目、文献来源、输出格式与引用规范,搜文献前再确认文献规模、年份跨度、来源门槛与语种配比,清单经核验后一次性写完整篇再输出;文献可用户已有材料抽取、自己粘贴或 AI 联网搜索,写入正文的每一篇都要有真实出处,正文里的方法名与数据只能来自实际读到的摘要或全文,读不到就只写到主题层面,既防编造引用也防编造结论;评述部分要求指出结论分歧、评估方法学局限、把研究空白落到具体对象与方法上;参考文献默认国标 GB/T 7714-2015;支持对话/Markdown/Word/LaTeX 输出,可选调用 Image2 生成文献分类框架图。本 skill 面向叙述性文献综述,不做元分析和统计合并,不代做 PRISMA 系统综述的筛选与偏倚评价。触发:文献综述、写综述、literature review、帮我写文献综述、国内外研究现状。
readme_snippet: 文献综述生成 Skill 按四部分推进一篇文献综述:研究背景与目的 → 文献梳理与分析 → 研究现状总结与评述 → 参考文献。 核心是前期对齐充分、文献真实可核验、结论不凭空补:开场把题目、文献来源、输出格式、引用规范一次性问清, 搜文献前再把检索口径定下来,文献清单经用户核验,然后一口气写完整篇初稿再交付,不再一段段停下来确认。 触发条件 用户要写文献综述 / 国内外研究现状 关键词:文献综述、写综述、literature review、帮我写文献综述、国内外研究现状 适用边界 做:叙述性文献综述、学位论文的国内外研究现状、期刊论文里的研究现状部分。 不做:元分析与统计合并(效应量、异质性检验、森林图),也不代替系统综述的文献筛选和偏倚风险评价。 用户在做系统综述时,本 skill 只负责把用户自己确认过的筛选数字画成 PRISMA 流程图, 不替用户判断纳入排除、不推算数字。数字不齐就留 n = ?,并在交付说明里列出待补项。 四条铁律 文献必须真:写入正文的每一篇文献都要有可核验来源。用户自己粘的照用;AI 搜的必须带出处链接、 先给用户核对,禁止凭记忆编造标题、作者、年份。 结论必须有依据:正文里写某篇文献"做了什么、得出什么",只能依据实际读到的原文——用户提供的摘要、 WebFetch 打开的摘要或全文页面。手里只有标题和年份的,就只写到主题层面(讨论了什么问题、属于哪条技术路线), 禁止补出原文没有的方法名、模型名、数据集、准确率和百分比。参考文献列表全真、正文转述半编, 比整条假引用更难查、危害更大。清单里每篇文献的证据等级在 Phase 1 标出来,写作时按等级决定能写多细。 前期对齐、一次成稿:干预集中在动笔之前——开场对齐、检索口径确认、文献清单核验。 这些过了之后,四部分连着一次性写完整篇,不再逐段停下来问用户。 先写主体:四部分里先写"文献梳理与分析",它定了全篇口径,之后回填背景、现状、参考文献才接得上。 这只是内部撰写顺序,不是分批交付。 交互总则:所有干预点一律走 AskUserQuestion 这个 skill 的人工干预必须用 AskUserQuestion 工具发起,不要用普通文字提问代替。凡是需要用户拍板、确认、 选择的地方,都调 AskUserQuestion,把选项列出来让用户点。下面每个 Phase 标了...

name: zpa-create-timeout-policy-rule
description: Create ZPA timeout policy rules that control session re-authentication and idle timeout behavior. Configures how long a user session remains active (reauth_timeout) and how long an idle session persists (reauth_idle_timeout) before requiring re-authentication. Supports conditions: APP, APP_GROUP, CLIENT_TYPE, SAML, SCIM, SCIM_GROUP, PLATFORM, and POSTURE. Use when an administrator asks: 'Set session timeout', 'Configure idle timeout', 'Require re-authentication after X hours', or 'Set different timeouts per app or user group.'
readme_snippet: ZPA: Create Timeout Policy Rule Keywords timeout policy, session timeout, idle timeout, reauth timeout, re-authentication, session expiry, idle disconnect, timeout rule, session duration, zpa timeout, reauth policy Overview Create ZPA timeout policy rules that define session re-authentication and idle timeout behavior. Timeout policies control how long a user's authenticated session remains valid and how long an idle connection persists before requiring re-authentication. Different applications and user groups can have different timeout values. Use this skill when: An administrator asks to configure session timeouts, set idle disconnect timers, require re-authentication after a specific period, or apply different timeout rules to different applications or user groups. --- Timeout Parameters reauthtimeout (Session Timeout) How long a user session remains valid before requiring re-authentication, regardless of activity.
